Carmen: Quick question — planning to switch payments-service from ALB TLS termination to TCP passthrough so pods can do mTLS. Anyone seen issues with sticky sessions or health checks? Thinking Gateway API passthrough + NLB or native NLB in front. pinging infra for terraform changes.
Devon: what's the main driver — latency or cert validation?
Carmen: certs. Pods validate client certs; ALB termination strips that. We need 1:1 client cert to pod.
Maya: passthrough is fine but ALB can't do L4 passthrough; NLB or AWS Gateway + NLB is typical. Health checks change from HTTP to TCP for TCP tgs.
Liam: Gateway API supports TLS mode Passthrough in our cluster, but we still need network LB in front. Terraform changes: aws_lb(load_balancer_type = "network") + target_group protocol = "TCP" and target_type = "ip".
Carmen: I sketched a terraform diff, can someone sanity-check? ```hcl
resource "aws_lb" "payments_nlb" {
  name               = "payments-nlb"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  subnets            = var.public_subnets
}
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "payments_tg" {
  name        = "payments-tg"
  port        = 443
  protocol    = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
}
```
Devon: quick notes: add health_check { protocol = "TCP" } and set deregistration_delay appropriately. Also ensure we're not enabling proxy protocol if we want raw client IP at pod. Update SGs for NodePort traffic if using node targets.
Maya: On k8s svc side, for passthrough we usually register pod ips (target_type ip) and keep Service type=ClusterIP; but controller semantics vary — some controllers expect NodePort to register nodes. Confirm with the AWS LB controller docs. Also secret handling: with passthrough the LB doesn't terminate TLS, so certificate secrets need to be on the pods. Gateway snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Gateway
spec:
  listeners:
  - name: tls
    port: 443
    protocol: TLS
    tls:
      mode: Passthrough
      certificateRefs: [] # passthrough ignores LB certs, ensure pods have certs
```
Liam: FYI controller accepts annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: \"nlb\"` or we can use GatewayClass to pick an NLB. Also confirm aws provider supports protocol on target group in your provider version.
Carmen: Thanks. @Devon can you review my terraform PR when you have a sec? https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 :eyes:
Devon: on it, will post comments tonight. Also tagging SRE for rollback plan.
sre-bot: IncidentRunbook: if we see 5xx spike or TLS handshake failures > 1% for 10m, revert to ALB termination by reverting commit abc123 and reapplying. :rotating_light:
Maya: ops note — do this as a canary: create NLB + new target group + gateway update in a canary namespace and shift 5% via routing rules. Test mTLS handshake against pods before shifting.
Carmen: Plan: create nlb + tg, update gateway to passthrough in canary, route 5% traffic, monitor healthchecks and TLS handshakes. If stable, promote to prod and decommission ALB config. I'll update PR to include healthcheck config and SG changes.
Devon: :thumbsup: I'll review and comment.
Liam: added lb_type and tg_protocol flags to the shared terraform module (internal link) — may need to bump module version in the PR.
Carmen: Great, thanks everyone. I'll push updates to the PR with healthcheck and security group changes later today.
